_comment: DOM contract between the Chrome extension and each AI site, plus what each site is good at and how much of it a student gets for free (the router reads `strengths` and `free_tier` to decide who answers what). Served live at GET /api/extension/config, so when a site renames a button you edit THIS FILE and every installed extension picks it up on its next run — no re-install. Selector lists are tried in order, first match wins. VERIFY THESE against the live sites before launch.

routing._comment: Fallback map used when the routing AI is unavailable or its daily free allowance is spent. When it IS available it sorts the whole bank in one call and picks per question. Nothing reassigns a question afterwards to even out load — except an assistant the student isn't signed into, or one that can't take the file uploads a document question needs. A LIST value rotates questions of that type across the sites named — theory is the bulk of every bank and carries no file, so it is shared between the two sites with unlimited text chat instead of piling on one. See _routing_evidence for why each type lands where it does.

chatgpt.label: ChatGPT
chatgpt.strengths: best at numerical working and step-by-step math — leads math reasoning benchmarks (AIME) — and writes clean LaTeX. Fast, and the clearest explainer of the four.
chatgpt.free_tier: unlimited text chat, but only 3 FILE UPLOADS PER DAY — so it is excellent for questions whose text is all you need, and nearly useless for questions that need the paper attached

claude.label: Claude
claude.strengths: best at long structured written answers, derivations, proofs and comparisons, and the strongest coder of the four (leads SWE-Bench Verified). Answers are the most complete and best organised — worth the most on a high-mark question.
claude.free_tier: the SMALLEST free allowance of the four — a compute pool that refills on 5-hour windows, around 15 messages in practice. Spend it on questions where depth earns marks, never on bulk. 5 file uploads per chat.

gemini.label: Gemini
gemini.strengths: best at anything visual or spatial — reading a graph, circuit, table or scanned page out of an attached document, and producing plots and diagrams. Recommended for visual STEM.
gemini.free_tier: compute-pooled with 5-hour resets, and generous with files: 10 uploads per prompt at 100 MB each. Good headroom for questions that need the paper attached.

kimi.label: Kimi
kimi._selector_note: UNVERIFIED against the live site — same status as the other three (see HANDOVER P0-1). Deliberately generic: the composer and send button are matched structurally so a class change doesn't break them.
kimi.strengths: slowest of the four, but the most patient with a long attached document — it reads a whole question paper without truncating it, and produces tables and plotted figures for questions built on data.
kimi.free_tier: no message cap and no upload cap on standard chat, on the current flagship model. The only site that can absorb a whole figure-heavy bank, so it carries the bulk.

_upload_note: How long to wait after attaching a file before pressing send. A chat site rejects a send while an upload is still in flight, and a big question paper takes seconds.
_routing_evidence: Routing is set from measured strengths AND free-tier capacity, checked August 2026. Capacity is the half everyone forgets and it is the half that breaks a 28-question run: ChatGPT gives unlimited text chat but only 3 FILE UPLOADS A DAY, and this product uploads the question paper once per question. Claude has the smallest free allowance of the four (a compute pool on 5-hour windows, ~15 messages in practice) and is also the best writer, so it gets the questions where depth actually earns marks rather than the bulk. Kimi's free tier has no message cap and no upload cap and reads long PDFs without truncating, which makes it the only site that can absorb a whole figure-heavy bank. Re-check these before launch: free tiers move every few months.
_document_sites_note: Document mode uploads the question paper once per question. Only sites that can take that volume belong near the front of this list — ChatGPT's 3-uploads-a-day free limit is spent before the first batch of three finishes, so it sits last and is used only when nothing else is available.
